summary: We designed a website containing an interactive story for kids aged 6-12 years old, teaching them about space and engineering while at the same time bringing awareness into all the discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars. This type of story's are crucial to children's development and they serve as a way to expand their creativeness, and their need of entertainment.
details:
Our project is an interactive story that aims to inform kids aged 6 to 12 about the hardware NASA has used in its missions and the impact it has had on science.

The story is narrated by KEPLER, an inactive space telescope that shares its own experience and that of other machines that participated in NASA missions, and that are now retired on the Moon, on Mars and in space.

The website was created with HTML (Hyper Text Markup Language), CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) and JavaScript while being hosted on neocities. All the sprites were drawn in Procreate.

Educational impact: It condenses real space history into one narrative (how the transit method finds exoplanets, what Spirit and Opportunity revealed about Mars’s watery past, and how the lunar rovers extended what Apollo astronauts could explore).
